title: Panic Restaurant
subtitle: EIM · Nintendo Entertainment System
summary: Panic Restaurant is EIM's NES platformer about a chef reclaiming his restaurant after a rival's curse brings its food to life. body: Panic Restaurant is EIM's NES platformer about a chef reclaiming his restaurant after a rival's curse brings its food to life. In the overseas edition, Cookie fights through six stages with kitchen utensils before confronting Ohdove. Familiar ingredients become animated enemies, giving the setting an immediately understandable joke. A kitchen is supposed to be somewhere the chef controls what happens to the food. Here, the food fights back, and the tools used to prepare it become the equipment needed to survive.

The overseas Cookie begins with a pan, while further equipment changes how he deals with the restaurant's hazards. The stages build their action around food and the spaces where it would normally be prepared or served. That consistency helps the absurd enemies belong to the same world. A dangerous dish can still be recognised as dinner, even while it approaches like a conventional platform-game opponent. The visual humour depends on that quick recognition, letting an ordinary object acquire another role without needing an explanation.

Kenji Eno designed the game before becoming better known for D and Enemy Zero. The Japanese edition stars Kokkun, whose default attack uses his head; localisation replaced it with Cookie's pan and changed other weapons and names. Taito published the game, which arrived late in the NES's life. Its character comes from applying one comic idea consistently: a restaurant has become an obstacle course, and the person best equipped to put it right is still the chef with the familiar tools.

A kitchen utensil becomes a weapon
A changed chef for the overseas menu
